summary:
The integrity half of the threat model is genuinely strong and should be preserved: treating the LLM as untrusted and letting the Lean kernel plus a deterministic gate (G0-G6, leanchecker, lake comparator statement-freeze, axiom audit) decide what counts as proved is the right spine, and it was exercised against real exploits. CSP is nonce-based with Shiki rendered through React (not innerHTML), verbatimPrompts:true blocks path/slash expansion of node text, settingSources:[] + strictMcpConfig isolate the run, the agent gets no Bash/web, the path guard is correctly a PreToolUse hook (always-on, unlike canUseTool), API-key env vars are stripped, and proposal virtual docs are not elaborated by the Lean server. Those are real strengths.

The confidentiality half, however, does not achieve what the docs claim, and I verified two holes by experiment on this machine. (1) The agent's own Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write run OUTSIDE bwrap with the user's full filesystem access and unmasked $HOME; their only confinement is a path guard specified as a pattern denylist ("shadow only; never lakefile*, .lake/**..."). cp -a preserves symlinks into the shadow, the design deliberately adds a .lake/packages symlink to the real tree, and a prefix/pattern check is bypassed by symlink traversal (verified: shadow/sub/evil -> /etc lets Read/Grep return /etc/passwd; the same vector reaches ~/.ssh and ~/.claude/.credentials.json). (2) The bwrap profile for agent-code builds uses --ro-bind / / without --clearenv and without masking /run, so the D-Bus session bus, Wayland, PipeWire, the keyring/gnupg dirs and VS Code's own IPC sockets stay reachable and DBUS/SSH_AUTH/WAYLAND env is inherited; I confirmed a connect() to the session bus succeeds inside the sandbox even though AF_INET is correctly blocked. The session bus reaches the Secret Service (gnome-keyring), so the "no $HOME, no network" containment the docs advertise is porous to stored secrets. The research containment test only checked write-outside/read-$HOME/DNS, so 03 §8.4 and D-25 overstate what was verified.

Two further gaps: accepted LLM code is thereafter elaborated UNSANDBOXED forever by both telelean's own lake build (03 §5 says the real-workspace build "needs no extra sandbox") and the vscode-lean4 server on open, with only a syntactic G0 denylist as the barrier — and 03's G0 list omits initialize/builtin_initialize, an arbitrary-IO-at-elaboration construct that r5's own list includes. On policy, the subscription reading is defensible and reasonably hedged for personal use, but it presents summarizer-approximate quotes as authoritative (r1 flagged this and told you to re-verify byte-exact) and does not reconcile Consumer Terms §3's "automated or non-human means ... except via an API Key" clause with driving the binary in an SDK agent loop. Fixes below are concrete and mostly cheap.

issues.section: §8.3 agent tool surface / §8.4 Shadow workspace; 02 D-25
issues.problem: The agent's built-in Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write run in the Claude Code process OUTSIDE bwrap, with the user's real uid, full filesystem access and an UNMASKED $HOME. Their only confinement is the PreToolUse hook, specified as a path-pattern denylist: pathGuard /* shadow only; never lakefile*, lean-toolchain, .lake/**, .telelean/frozen/** */. Nothing in any doc says the hook canonicalizes paths (realpath) before the containment/deny test. This is bypassable: (a) §8.4 copies the workspace with `cp -a`, which preserves symlinks, so any symlink already in the user's repo is reproduced in the shadow pointing at its real absolute target; (b) the design DELIBERATELY adds a `.lake/packages` symlink in the shadow pointing to the real workspace. A prefix/glob check on the raw input path then permits a path that resolves outside the shadow. Because $HOME is not masked for this process, a repo symlink to ~/.ssh or ~/.claude/.credentials.json lets the agent (or a prompt-injected agent) read SSH keys / Claude credentials and write them verbatim into a node body the user later reviews. Verified locally: `cp -a` preserved `sub/evil -> /etc`; a startsWith(shadowRoot) check ALLOWED `shadow/sub/evil/passwd` while realpath escaped to /etc/passwd and `head` returned the root line.
issues.evidence: verified-locally (this review): cp -a preserves symlinks into the shadow; prefix-containment passes while realpath('shadow/sub/evil/passwd') = /etc/passwd. Cross-ref r5 ّInput packaging/Agent tool surfaceّ (agent Reads/Greps the shadow; hook description is a denylist, no realpath); r5 risk ّsession transcripts... per shadow cwdّ shows read output also egresses to Anthropic. Docs grep confirms no occurrence of realpath/canonical/symlink-resolution for the guard.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the guard containment-based, not pattern-based: for every tool call (and for each path/glob base/grep root) compute fs.realpathSync of the target and require it to be inside fs.realpathSync(shadowRoot); reject if resolution fails or leaves the shadow. Resolve BEFORE matching deny patterns. Do not put a .lake/packages symlink in the shadow that the agent can traverse: either exclude .lake from the agent-visible tree entirely and bind packages read-only only inside the bwrap build, or replace the symlink with a bind that the realpath check still rejects for agent tools. Strip/flatten symlinks when building the shadow (cp -aL into a dedicated model-files-only tree, or copy only *.lean + lakefile + toolchain + manifest and refuse symlinked entries). Additionally deny reads of dotfiles/dot-dirs by default. Treat $HOME as unmasked for this process and design accordingly.

issues.section: §8.4 Sandbox for every Lean run; 02 D-25; §14 risk row
issues.problem: The bwrap profile for building agent-written Lean is `bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs $HOME --ro-bind ~/.elan ~/.elan --bind $SHADOW $SHADOW --chdir $SHADOW --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session ... lake build`. `--ro-bind / /` exposes the ENTIRE real filesystem read-only and there is no `--clearenv`. The docs advertise this as ّno network, no $HOME and a memory capّ (D-25) and ّVerified to contain an agent run_cmd that wrote outside the project, listed $HOME and resolved DNSّ. That containment is porous: --tmpfs /tmp masks the X11 pathname socket, but /run is still bound, so /run/user/$UID/{bus (D-Bus session bus), wayland-0, pipewire-0, keyring, gnupg} and VS Code's own IPC sockets remain present, and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS/SSH_AUTH_SOCK/WAYLAND_DISPLAY are inherited. --unshare-all unshares the network namespace (AF_INET blocked, good) but does NOT isolate pathname AF_UNIX sockets. The D-Bus session bus reaches the Secret Service (gnome-keyring org.freedesktop.secrets), app launching, and portals; Wayland/PipeWire reach screen/audio; the VS Code sockets reach the editor. So building untrusted agent code can talk to the keyring and other session services despite $HOME being masked. The research test (write-outside / read-$HOME / DNS) did not cover sockets, so 03 §8.4/D-25's ّcontainedّ claim is overstated.
issues.evidence: verified-locally (this review): under the exact isolation core, /run/user/1002/{bus,wayland-0,pipewire-0} show as VISIBLE sockets, keyring+gnupg dirs VISIBLE, 5 vscode IPC sockets visible, DBUS/SSH_AUTH/WAYLAND env inherited; a python3 AF_UNIX connect() to /run/user/1002/bus SUCCEEDED while create_connection to 1.1.1.1:53 was blocked (OSError). Host `ls /run/user/1002` confirms the sockets and `srw-rw-rw- bus`.
issues.suggested_fix: Prefer an allowlist mount model over `--ro-bind / /`: bind only what Lean needs (--ro-bind /usr, /bin, /lib*, /etc/ssl or specific files, ~/.elan toolchain, --proc/--dev), and NEVER bind /run. If you keep `--ro-bind / /`, add `--tmpfs /run` (and explicitly `--tmpfs "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"`). Always `--clearenv` and then set only HOME, PATH, and any LAKE/ELAN vars needed; drop DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY, WAYLAND_DISPLAY. Re-run the containment test with explicit socket/keyring probes (attempt D-Bus/ssh-agent/Wayland connect, expect failure) and add them to the exploits/ fixture gate. Reconcile the two differing profiles (03 §8.4 vs r5): 03's also omits the read-only packages bind and the explicit --setenv HOME/PATH.

issues.problem: Everything before Accept is careful, but §5 says the real-workspace refresh ّruns lake build in the real workspace. That is your code, which your Lean server already elaborates, so it needs no extra sandbox.ّ After Accept, that code was written by the untrusted LLM. From then on it is elaborated UNSANDBOXED on every refresh by telelean's own SemanticRunner and on every open by the vscode-lean4 server, both of which run arbitrary code during elaboration (verified elsewhere that #eval/run_cmd execute at elaboration). The sole barrier is the accept-time G0 lint, a TS token scan — a syntactic denylist, which is inherently incomplete for a macro-rich elaborator. Concretely, 03 §8.5's G0 row and D-27's G0 list enumerate #eval/run_cmd/macros/notation/elab, set_option debug.*, native_decide, implemented_by/extern/unsafe, new imports, lakefile/toolchain edits — but OMIT `initialize`/`builtin_initialize`, which run arbitrary IO at module load/elaboration and are present in r5's own G0 list. A construct that passes G0 (e.g. an `initialize` block, or a future unlisted elaboration hook) then executes unsandboxed forever post-accept.
issues.evidence: documented in docs (03 §5 quote; §8.5 G0 row text; D-27 G0 list) cross-checked against r5 ّG0 lint (text)ّ which additionally lists `initialize/builtin_initialize`; r1/r5 verified-locally that Lean elaboration runs arbitrary IO (#eval wrote a file). Gap is a denylist-omission plus an unsandboxed execution path.
issues.suggested_fix: Run telelean's own real-workspace lake build / extractor inside the SAME bwrap profile (post-SEC-SANDBOX fix) always — the toolchain is identical and the only cost is that the user's own saves are also sandboxed, which is acceptable and arguably desirable. Treat G0 as defense-in-depth, never as the boundary. Reconcile the G0 denylist with r5's fuller list (add initialize/builtin_initialize, deriving-with-handler, set_option maxHeartbeats 0 / maxRecDepth DoS, attribute assignments). Surface an explicit one-time warning at Accept that the vscode-lean4 server (which telelean cannot sandbox) will elaborate accepted LLM code unsandboxed when those files are opened.

issues.problem: Two read/exfil surfaces are not covered by the stated guard. (a) `check_lean({files?})` takes a caller-supplied files list; r5's hook matcher is 'Read|Edit|Write|Glob|Grep' and does NOT include mcp__telelean__check_lean, so the files param is unguarded. Inside the build sandbox `--ro-bind / /` exposes the whole FS, so an absolute or ../ path (or a path resolving through the packages symlink) can point the extractor/build at real files outside the shadow; their pretty-printed types, docstrings and diagnostics then come back in the facts JSON shown to the user and written to the transcript (which egresses to Anthropic). (b) Glob and Grep RETURN FILE CONTENTS/paths as matches; combined with SEC-PATHGUARD-SYMLINK (no realpath), Grep over a symlinked-out subtree is a direct content-exfil channel into the transcript and the UI. The design frames the guard as integrity (ّuntrustedّ writes) but under-treats it as a confidentiality/exfil control.
issues.evidence: docs: 03 §8.3 check_lean row + r5 tool schema (files?); r5 harness matcher 'Read|Edit|Write|Glob|Grep' excludes check_lean. Builds on this review's verified symlink traversal and the --ro-bind / / exposure. r5 risk notes transcripts persist per shadow cwd under ~/.claude/projects (egress).
issues.suggested_fix: Validate check_lean.files in the tool handler: resolve each via realpath, require containment in the shadow, reject absolute/.. and anything under .lake/.telelean/frozen; default to the run's target modules. Give Glob/Grep the same realpath-containment treatment as Read (extract the path/glob-base/grep-root from each tool input and canonicalize). Cap and scope what facts/diagnostics are returned to declarations within the shadow model modules. Document that tool output is part of what leaves the machine.

issues.problem: The subscription reading (personal use on the unmodified binary is the documented lane; sharing needs API keys/approval; strip API-key env; never --bare; never touch credentials) is defensible and the user's intent is personal use — but two accuracy issues. (1) D-23 presents the policy text in quotation marks as authoritative, yet r1 explicitly recorded that these quotes ّcame through a summarizing fetch rather than byte-exact retrievalّ and listed ّAre the policy quotes byte-exact? Re-check the live pages before quoting externallyّ as an open question; that caveat is dropped in the design docs. (2) The reading leans entirely on the legal-page carve-out about an end user ّsigning in to the unmodified Claude Code binaryّ, but does not reconcile Consumer Terms §3 (r1: access ّthrough automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise is prohibited except via an Anthropic API Key or where Anthropic explicitly permitsّ) with the fact that telelean programmatically drives that binary in an SDK agent loop. The residual tension is real and under-played in a doc the user will rely on to make a go/no-go call.
issues.evidence: documented: r1 findings/risks/open-questions ('quotes came through a summarizing fetch'; 'Are the policy quotes byte-exact?'); r1 Consumer Terms §3 finding; r5 'Policy ambiguity around subscription (OAuth) use through the Agent SDK'. D-23 and 03 §8/§14 present the quotes without the re-verify caveat and without the §3 reconciliation.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the r1 caveat verbatim ('policy wording is summarizer-approximate; verify byte-exact against the live overview + legal pages, dated, before relying on it'). Add one sentence reconciling Consumer Terms §3: note that telelean orchestrates the unmodified binary automatically and that the personal-use position rests on the legal-page carve-out, so this is the user's risk decision; re-confirm in writing with Anthropic before any sharing. Keep the correct notes already present (SDK is named in the policy so 'CLI not SDK' is no escape; --bare never reads OAuth; API-key backend before distribution).

issues.section: D-23 egress note (IC-34); 03 §8.3 context bundle; D-12 sessions
issues.problem: D-23 acknowledges ّThe run also sends your beliefs and Lean files to Anthropicّ, but under-scopes it. The §8.3 context bundle includes a ّcompact index of ALL nodesّ (every node's verbatim natural_name), the vocabulary, recorded DECISIONs and target files, and the agent then Reads shadow source on demand — so the whole mental model, not just the selection, leaves on every run. The independent back-translation is a SECOND Claude session (more egress). And per r5, session transcripts are stored under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded shadow cwd>/*.jsonl, persist after the shadow is deleted, and accumulate one directory per run (shadow cwd is unique per run id) — an unbounded local store of the user's beliefs and file contents that .telelean/.gitignore does not cover because it lives in $HOME.
issues.evidence: docs: 03 §8.3 'a compact index of all nodes'; D-10/§8 back-translation 'fresh session'; r5 risk 'Session transcripts are stored per shadow cwd under ~/.claude/projects. Deleting shadows does not delete transcripts.' IC-34 in 01.
issues.suggested_fix: State plainly in D-23/user-guide that the entire model index (all natural_name text), vocabulary, decisions and read files are transmitted per run, and that back-translation doubles that. Offer a setting to scope the index (IC-32 already calls for sending only the relevant part). Add transcript hygiene: a stable per-project shadow cwd (so ~/.claude/projects does not grow one dir per run) or a cleanup that removes the per-run transcript when its shadow is pruned; document where transcripts live.

issues.problem: The webview correctly renders Shiki tokens through React (not innerHTML) and uses a nonce CSP, and the docs state workspace text + LLM output are untrusted — good. But node cards render a Markdown body (the '---' section), and neither 03 §7 nor r3 specifies HOW the Markdown is rendered. A Markdown→HTML path can still introduce javascript: / data: links on anchors, auto-linked URLs, or raw HTML passthrough even under a nonce CSP (CSP blocks remote scripts/img but not a user-clicked javascript: URI or a crafted link). Body text is attacker-influenceable (a cloned repo's .lean file, or an agent-authored node).
issues.evidence: docs: 03 §3.2 'body after ---' Markdown; §7 'Shiki tokens are rendered through React, never innerHTML'; r3 CSP 'img-src cspSource data:' blocks remote images. No doc names the Markdown renderer or its sanitization policy.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify a Markdown renderer configured with raw-HTML disabled and a URL sanitizer that allows only http/https/mailto (and relative), rejecting javascript:/data:/vbscript: on links; render to React elements, not innerHTML. Keep img-src without remote origins (no https:) so images can't beacon. Add a webview test asserting a body containing [x](javascript:alert(1)) and an is neutralized.

strengths: Correct core trust posture: LLM is untrusted and a deterministic gate on the Lean kernel decides proof validity (G0-G6, leanchecker kernel replay for skipKernelTC, lake comparator statement-freeze + permitted_axioms, axiom audit with loadExts:=false so initializers don't run). This integrity design is strong and was exercised against real exploits.

PreToolUse hook is the right mechanism for the always-on path guard (it runs before allow rules and even in permissive modes), rather than canUseTool which auto-approved calls bypass. The concept is right; only the implementation detail (realpath containment) is missing.

Agent has no Bash, no WebFetch/WebSearch, no subagents, no AskUserQuestion; settingSources:[] + strictMcpConfig isolate the run from the user's global CLAUDE.md/hooks/MCP; this removes whole classes of exfiltration and injection.
verbatimPrompts:true prevents a node's natural_name like '@/etc/passwd' or '/command' from being expanded by the CLI — a real prompt-injection mitigation.

Credential handling: strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, never reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json, never --bare; subscription login is used via the unmodified binary.

Network is genuinely blocked in the sandbox (AF_INET fails; verified), and the sandbox fails closed if bwrap is missing. systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G gives a real cgroup memory cap (good for the RAM-sensitive user).
Nonce CSP with no unsafe-eval, Shiki rendered through React not innerHTML, remote images blocked; the docs explicitly treat workspace text and LLM output as untrusted in the webview.

The independent back-translation runs in a fresh, tool-less session (no exfil surface), and proposal virtual docs use a non-file scheme that the Lean server does not elaborate (verified in r6) — both thoughtful.

G5 markup policy enforces byte-identical natural_name/rationale and origin:agent marking, so prompt injection cannot silently rewrite the user's specification or launder agent assumptions as user beliefs.
questions_for_user: Where does VS Code put the extension global storage that holds <storage>/runs/<id>/ws on this snap install (likely ~/snap/code/common/... under $HOME)? The bwrap ordering (--tmpfs $HOME then --bind $SHADOW) only works if the shadow path is re-bound after the tmpfs; confirm the real path so the profile is correct.

Do you rely on CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or a non-default credential location? r1 notes that stripping/relocating it signs the agent out, so telelean should leave your real one intact (not point it at the shadow) — but it should still never read the credential file. Which is it for your setup?

Is this machine ever multi-user, and do you mount external or network volumes (/mnt, /media, /srv, NFS/SMB)? Under --ro-bind / / those are readable inside the build sandbox; an allowlist mount model would exclude them.

Will telelean ever be shared, pushed to a public repo, or run for anyone but you? That flips the policy answer (API keys / Anthropic approval) and means the proprietary SDK + ~330MB binary must not be vendored/published (keep node_modules gitignored; package.json already private:true).

Is it acceptable to also run your OWN real-workspace lake build/extractor inside the sandbox (slightly slower refreshes) so that accepted LLM code is contained on every subsequent elaboration, not just at accept time?
